insights.headline: Gold steadies near $3,883 after its worst week in months as Fed hike bets lift the dollar
insights.summary: Spot gold steadied near $3,883 an ounce on Friday after Thursday's steep losses, closing the week down about 4.5% — its worst week in four months — as hot US inflation lifted bets on further Fed tightening and pushed the dollar to a 19-month high. MCX gold stayed near Rs 1.37 lakh per 10 g, while silver slipped below $50. In India, jewellery exports jumped 34% in October, even as gold imports fell 62% on the year.
points: Spot gold near $3,883, down about 4.5% on the week — its worst week in four months — after hot US inflation lifted Fed hike bets.
Gold futures gave back about 90% of Friday's rally to $3,927 and ended near a 20-week low, InvestingLive reports.
Goldman Sachs cut its end-2026 gold target to $4,150 from $4,650 and its 2027 target to $4,800, citing the Fed's hawkish shift.
BofA now expects Fed hikes in December, January and March after hot October CPI; markets price an almost 90% chance of a December move.
Central banks bought 321 tonnes of gold in Q3, up 42% on the year, even as prices slid below $4,000, World Gold Council data show.

brief.headline: Gold steadies near $3,883 after worst week in months
brief.summary: Spot gold steadied near $3,883 after a 4.5% weekly fall on Fed hike bets; MCX gold stayed near Rs 1.37 lakh per 10 g.

bullets.text: Hot US inflation lifted Fed hike bets and pushed the dollar to a 19-month high, leaving gold set for its worst week in four months.
Jewellery exports jumped 34% in October as gold imports fell 62% on the year; Delhi gold eased as post-Diwali demand faded.
Next test: the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, with markets pricing an almost 90% chance of a quarter-point rise.

trending.title: Fed hike bets drive gold's worst week in months
trending.summary: Hot October inflation has traders pricing more Fed tightening, lifting the dollar and yields and pushing gold to its worst week in four months, with banks now pencilling in hikes into early 2027.

trending.title: India buys the dip as imports fall
trending.summary: Jewellery exports jumped 34% in October and gold imports fell 62% on the year as the global correction bit, while Delhi gold eased for a fourth session as post-Diwali demand faded.

trending.title: Silver's deficit story meets a hawkish Fed
trending.summary: Silver slid about 3.8% on the week despite a sixth straight annual supply deficit, as fund selling and higher yields outweigh jewellery demand.

trending.title: MCX steadies near Rs 1.37 lakh
trending.summary: MCX gold rebounded after the week's sharp fall and silver lagged, with the rupee offering little relief as the dollar held near a 19-month high.

trending.title: Major gold discoveries are drying up
trending.summary: Only nine deposits found since 2020 met S&P Global's major-discovery bar, holding 38 million ounces combined, against 371 deposits and 3.2 billion ounces from 1990 to 2025.

items.title: Gold posts steep weekly loss as Treasury yields rise, Fed tightening bets persist
items.summary: Spot gold steadied near $3,883 an ounce on Friday after Thursday's steep losses, but still ended the week sharply lower as hot US inflation, rising Treasury yields and bets on further Fed tightening weighed on bullion. Silver fell 2.6% to about $48.63. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, annual PPI hit 6.5%, and markets priced an 89% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike in December.

items.title: Gold futures rose Friday, but the rally failed. What I'm watching next week
items.summary: Gold futures ended Friday at $3,887.6 an ounce, slightly higher after surrendering about 90% of an early rally to $3,927.2, and closed the week down about 4.7%; the $3,856.7 low was a fresh 20-week low. Higher yields and a stronger dollar pressured bullion, and both Thursday and Friday closed above the October 30 low of $3,879.3, what the author calls a possible sign of stabilisation.

items.title: Rate-hike bets keep gold on track for worst week in four months
items.summary: Spot gold held near $3,880 an ounce on Friday, up 0.1% after briefly touching $3,923 on the US producer-price data, and stayed set for a weekly drop of about 4.5%, its worst week since early June. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, below the 0.4% forecast, and traders put December quarter-point hike odds at 91.4%. Silver fell 1.9% to $49.05 an ounce, also headed for a weekly loss.

items.title: Goldman Sachs cuts year-end gold price target to $4,150/oz, 2027 target to $4,800/oz
items.summary: Goldman Sachs cut its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150 an ounce from $4,650 and its end-2027 target to $4,800 from $5,400, blaming the Fed's hawkish shift for weaker investor demand. The bank still expects central banks to buy about 60 tonnes a month through 2027 and sees rate cuts from late 2027 supporting gold later.

items.title: BofA adds January Fed hike to forecast, says quarterly pace no longer enough
items.summary: Bank of America added a 25-basis-point January 2027 rate hike to its Fed forecast, now expecting increases in December, January and March after October CPI came in hot for a third straight month. Markets price an almost 90% chance of a December hike, with a small chance of a 50-basis-point move.

items.title: Central Bank Gold Buying Surges 42% as Prices Dip Below US$4,000
items.summary: Central banks bought 321 tonnes of gold in the third quarter, up 42% on the year and the most since late 2024, World Gold Council data show, even as prices slid below $4,000. China and Poland led reported buying, while about 63% of official demand was unreported; purchases in the first nine months reached 675 tonnes.

items.title: Oil and gold imports push India's October trade deficit to US$39.88 billion
items.summary: India's merchandise trade deficit widened to a one-year high of $39.88 billion in October as festive gold buying and higher oil costs lifted imports nearly 20% from September. Gold imports rose to $5.51 billion from $1.80 billion in September, while exports hit a record $49.47 billion.

items.title: India's October gold imports plunge 62.57% to $5.51 billion amid global price correction
items.summary: India's gold imports fell 62.57% from a year earlier to $5.51 billion in October, Commerce Department data showed, with prices below $4,000 an ounce; April-October imports were down 39.9% at $24.78 billion. The World Gold Council said gold may be nearing a temporary bottom after ending October at $3,913 an ounce, down 6.3% in the month.

items.title: Gold Prices Hit Records. Where Are the Major Discoveries?
items.summary: Only nine gold deposits discovered between 2020 and 2025 reached S&P Global's major-discovery threshold, holding a combined 38 million ounces — a fraction of the 371 deposits and roughly 3.2 billion ounces found from 1990 to 2025 — even as gold cleared $5,000 an ounce early in 2026, underscoring how thin the long-term supply pipeline has become.

items.title: Gold Price Jumps By Rs 1,300, But Rate Still Below Rs 1,37,000 On MCX
items.summary: Gold futures rose Rs 455, or 0.33%, to Rs 1,36,680 per 10 grams, after rising as much as Rs 1,362 to an intraday high of Rs 1,37,587. Silver futures fell Rs 750, or 0.42%, to Rs 1,77,974 per kg. Gold had risen 46% in 2026 before the recent correction, NDTV Profit reports.

items.title: Gold Prices Fall to Rs 1.40 Lakh Per 10 Grams as Post-Diwali Demand Weakens
items.summary: Gold fell Rs 2,500 to Rs 1,40,900 per 10 grams in Delhi on Friday, a fourth straight session of losses, as weak global cues and fading demand after Diwali weighed on prices. Silver fell Rs 3,500 to Rs 1,84,000 per kg. HDFC Securities' Saumil Gandhi cited soft retail demand, a stronger dollar and rising US yields.

items.title: India Bullion: Down as dollar hits 19-month high; hawkish Fed also weighs
items.summary: Gold and silver futures on MCX and COMEX fell for a third straight session as the dollar rose to a 19-month high above 103 and traders fully priced a December Fed rate rise. At 18:49 IST, MCX December gold stood at Rs 1,41,185 per 10 g and silver at Rs 1,80,800 per kg; jewellers cut domestic discounts to Rs 500 as lower prices drew buying, with the rupee at 94.04 per dollar.

items.title: Gold rebounds after sharp fall, silver lags: What should Indian investors watch
items.summary: MCX December gold rose 0.39% to Rs 1.36 lakh per 10 g as bargain hunting followed Thursday's slide, while silver eased 0.14% to Rs 1.78 lakh per kg; spot gold gained 1.1% to $3,918.59 an ounce.

items.title: Silver demand seen down 5% this year due to weaker jewellery purchases
items.summary: Silver demand is expected to fall 5% in 2026 to 1.08 billion ounces, Metals Focus told Reuters, as weaker jewellery demand and substitution in solar cells bite. Jewellery demand is forecast down 22% and silverware down 17%, with high prices and weak rural spending in India pushing buyers to smaller pieces. ETP selling of 45 million ounces this year has eased tightness in the physical market.

items.title: Silver's 6th Annual Deficit Masks a Surplus as ETF Selling Adds Supply
items.summary: Metals Focus and the Silver Institute now expect a sixth straight annual silver deficit of 35 million ounces in 2026, narrower than the 46.3 million ounces forecast in April. But silver funds are expected to release 45 million ounces over the year, flipping the balance to a 10 million ounce surplus. Coin and bar demand is forecast at 215 million ounces, down 2%.

items.title: India's gem and jewellery exports jump 34% to $2.92 billion in October on festive demand
items.summary: India's gem and jewellery exports surged 34.01% year on year to $2.92 billion in October, from $2.18 billion a year earlier, per GJEPC data. In rupee terms shipments rose 44.71% to Rs 27,862.82 crore, led by gold jewellery, silver jewellery and lab-grown diamonds on strong orders ahead of the Christmas and year-end holiday season.

items.title: India's forex reserves rise by $2.49 billion to $719.55 billion: RBI data
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves rose $2.49 billion to $719.55 billion in the week ended November 6, the RBI's weekly data showed, recovering after two straight weekly declines. The value of the RBI's gold holdings rose $2.21 billion to $104.80 billion.

items.title: SGB 2018-19 Series III final redemption today: Investors to earn up to 348% return; check RBI fixed price, interest rate
items.summary: The RBI has fixed the final redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2018-19 Series-III at ₹14,024 per unit as the tranche matures on November 13, 2026, eight years after issue. Holders who bought at ₹3,183 a gram gain about 341%, and online buyers at ₹3,133 up to 348%, before the 2.5% annual interest.
